en.title: Nearer, My God, to Thee
en.author: Sarah Flower Adams
stanzas:
[E]Nearer, my God, to [B7]Thee, nearer to [E]Thee!
E'en [E]though it be a [A]cross that [B7]raiseth [E]me,
Still [A]all my song shall [E]be, nearer, my [B7]God, to [E]Thee.

Or, if on joyful wing cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot, upward I'll fly,
Still all my song shall be, nearer, my God, to Thee.

notes: Text from Timeless Truths, which credits stanza 6 ("There in my Father's home") to Edward H. Bickersteth, Jr. — it is not Adams's and many hymnals print only her five. It is common enough in gospel hymnals to keep, but drop it if the maintainer wants Adams's text alone. The 'chorus' here is not a true refrain: it is the tune's closing phrase, which every stanza repeats. Timeless Truths prints it separately for that reason; hymnary's United Methodist Hymnal text instead sets it as the last line inside each stanza. Either way it is sung once per stanza, which is what the shells do with a chorus. Hymnary's line division for the same text is eight short lines (hence the 6.4.6.4.6.6.6.4 meter recorded here); this source's three long lines are the same words. Year: 1841 per Timeless Truths and the worklist; hymnary's authority page says 1840. Key: BETHANY is F major on hymnary's tune page and in the Timeless Truths score; E is the nearest guitar key (1 semitone down). Independently cross-checked 2026-08-01 against Wikipedia, which corroborates Adams's five stanzas, Lowell Mason's 1856 BETHANY, and that the sixth stanza was added later by Edward Henry Bickersteth Jr. — so the stanza-6 caveat above is confirmed, not merely asserted by one source. Variant in stanza 5: several hymnals (the United Methodist Hymnal among them) read "upward I fly" where this source has "upward I'll fly"; the same printings give "steps unto heaven" and "in mercy given" unelided, but the elided "Heav'n"/"giv'n" kept here are what BETHANY's 6.4 lines actually scan to. Re-verified 2026-08-02 against hymnal.net (no. 614), a fourth independent site: its stanzas 1 and 4 match this file word-for-word, and its piano key is F major — further support for the E-guitar-key derivation. Its house text diverges materially in stanza 2 ("Though, like a wanderer, / The sun gone down, / Darkness comes over me" for this file's "Though like the wanderer... Darkness be over me" — Adams's 1841 original has "the wanderer" and "Darkness be") and replaces stanza 3's opening couplet with "There let me see the sight, / An open heaven"; it prints neither stanza 5 nor the Bickersteth stanza. This file's readings stand with Timeless Truths and the mainstream hymnal text.
